summary: generalized_adhesion implements F = -w*pi*R_eff*deltan for deltan>0 only (verified to 1e-10 N in a 2-type test). This is not JKR/DMT: zero force at deltan=0, no tensile regime, no pull-off/hysteresis. With Hooke it is exactly a stiffness reduction kn -> kn - w*pi*R* (never net-attractive unless w*pi*R*>kn, then unbounded interpenetration). With Hertz the net force is attractive only for deltan < (w*pi*R*/K)^2 with max pull-off 4c^3/(27K^2), c=w*pi*R*. Damping is still computed from the unreduced kn, so the realised e differs from the input e. For F in N the parameter must have units Pa (J/m^3), not J/m^2 as the name 'adhesionEnergy' suggests.
failure_scenario: User enters a JKR work of adhesion w = 0.05 J/m^2 for 1 mm glass beads: force ~ 0.05*pi*5e-4*deltan ~ 1e-9 N (no measurable cohesion, no agglomeration), while JKR pull-off 1.5*pi*w*R* ~ 1.2e-4 N. chute_wear_hpc uses adh=15 -> negligible effect.
recommendation: Rename the parameter (e.g. adhesionStressDensity [Pa]) or re-implement as a documented JKR/DMT family: DMT F=-2*pi*w*R* constant in contact plus an outer range; JKR with pull-off -1.5*pi*w*R* and hysteretic separation at delta_c (Thornton & Ning 1998; LAMMPS pair granular 'jkr'/'dmt'). Add pull-off V&V (request V-06).

summary: For superquadrics the model uses the volume-equivalent radius (pair_gran_base.h:268) instead of the curvature-based sidata.reff that the normal models use, and adds no torque about the contact point (normal models add xci x Fn under NONSPHERICAL_ACTIVE_FLAG), so the claim 'valid for superquadric' is not supported.

recommendation: Use sidata.reff when is_non_spherical; add torque = (contact_point - x_i) x F_coh (and for j); add a superquadric pull-off/torque test.

summary: Report caveat (sections 8/13/14.2) refuted: at vrel==0 and gammat==0 (also gammat<0, gammat=inf, Fn=0, NaN inputs) old and new return the identical gamma. The rewrite is NOT bitwise identical in general: (a) branch flips within +-4 ulp of the tie Ft_friction==gammat*vrel (4.1-4.5% of tie samples); (b) with -O3 -march=native (FMA contraction, GCC default for C++) 2.8% of random physical samples differ by <=2 ulp; (c) overflow when gammat*vrel > ~1.3e154 or underflow of squares < ~1e-154 selects the unscaled branch (e.g. Coulomb cap not applied at 1e200 N). At -O2 random physical samples are bitwise identical (0/2e7).
failure_scenario: Only ULP-level trajectory divergence (chaotic amplification) between HEAD and modified builds; never a physically visible difference in realistic ranges.
recommendation: Label as 'equivalent up to rounding'. If bitwise identity with HEAD is wanted: 'if (gammat>0 && vrelsq>0) { const double vrel=sqrt(vrelsq); if (Ft_friction < gammat*vrel) gamma = Ft_friction/vrel; }' keeps the sqrt saving at vrel==0 and is identical to HEAD for all finite inputs.

summary: [LEGACY] Frame indifference is only partial: the history is projected onto the current tangent plane each step (:155-158) but not rescaled to keep its magnitude and not rotated with the pair's spin about the normal. The spring is the total form Ft=-kt(delta)*s with kt=8G*sqrt(R*delta) re-evaluated every step (:166), which is non-incremental Mindlin and non-conservative under varying delta.
failure_scenario: Elastic oblique impact (e=1, gammat=0): tangential spring energy changes with delta without work -> energy creation/destruction; rebound spin differs from Maw-Barber-Fawcett/Thornton 2013 reference; a sphere pair spinning about the contact normal keeps a lab-fixed spring direction.
evidence_ref: Thornton, Cummins & Cleary (2011, 2013); Di Renzo & Di Maio (2004); LAMMPS GRANULAR tangential mindlin (rotate+rescale, incremental option)
recommendation: Offer an incremental Mindlin option (dFt = -kt*ds, with the rescale-on-unloading rule of Thornton 2013) and rotate+rescale history (as LAMMPS). Accept by V-02 oblique impact and V-04 energy budget.

summary: [LEGACY] The Coulomb check applies to the spring force only; in the stick branch the damping term is added afterwards, so |Ft| = |kt s + gammat vt| can exceed mu*|Fn|.

recommendation: Cap the total tangential force (LAMMPS GRANULAR does Fscrit on the total, then back-computes the spring).

summary: [LEGACY] For walls radj:=radi, so rEff=radi/2 (sphere-plane R* should be radi): the viscous normal/tangential forces against walls are halved. Soulie fit constant C keeps F~0.03-0.06*2piR*gamma at the rupture distance -> force jump at rupture.

summary: [LEGACY] EPSD rolling-spring history (r_torque_old) is never projected/rotated onto the current tangent plane; with torsionTorque off only the increment is tangential, so after the contact normal rotates the stored torque acquires a spurious torsional component.

recommendation: Project c_history onto the tangent plane (and rescale) each step, as for the tangential spring.
